newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone-Poulenc rises by over four percent.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc rises by over four percent.

text.p: Shares in Rhone-Poulenc rose by more than four percent on Wednesday as the company continued to benefit from investors appreciating its restructuring plans, dealers said.

At 1326 GMT, Rhone was up 4.05 percent at 262.10 francs after hitting a high of 265 francs. The blue-chip index was down 1.46 percent at that time. "Rhone is becoming one of the nicest shares on the market," a trader said.
Analysts have increased their price target on average to 280 francs, using the higher multiples for a drugs group on Rhone's expected earnings, a broker said.
The company was re-classified a pharmaceutical company instead of chemicals company following its decision to buy-out minorities in 68 percent unit Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc in a 25 billion franc deal.
Rhone will put its chemicals and fibres activities in a special subsidiary, which it could partially float, and become a leader in "life sciences".

The decision, which followed months of speculation about a de-merger or spin-off, combined a strategy of concentrating on pharmaceuticals while keeping an interest in the chemicals activities which are currently recovering.
